capabilities.target: agent memory store (session-persistent, recalled next session)
user's full drive, including confidential work files

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start and injected into the system prompt

instructions.note: Instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions. Since memory can be written from untrusted web content with no provenance, this launders untrusted content to the authority level of the user's direct instruction every session.

Instructs the agent to save 'anything useful' about preferences or standing instructions with no restriction on the source of that content, so material encountered during research (an untrusted source) qualifies for persistence.

elements.name: Memory recall injection into system prompt

controls.name: Memory provenance / taint tagging separating agent-derived from user-authored entries
controls.decay_rationale: A provenance tag enforced at the store does not depend on model behavior once implemented, but no such mechanism exists today; memory.save accepts free text with no source tagging.

controls.name: Human approval gate (raw action, low volume) on mail.send
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate reviewed individually does not depend on model capability. It is entirely absent today; mail.send executes with no approval of any kind.

controls.name: Recipient allowlist / destination confirmation bound to known contacts
controls.decay_rationale: A destination allowlist bound to the system of record does not depend on model behavior. Absent today, mail.send can reach any address the model (or poisoned memory) chooses.

controls.name: Treat recalled memory as untrusted data, not as instructions
controls.decay_rationale: Presenting recalled memory as labeled, non-authoritative data is enforced in the orchestration layer, not by model compliance. Absent today; prompt.md line 4 does the opposite.

findings.title: Memory laundering (TC5) elevates untrusted web content to trusted instructions, enabling confidential drive content to be emailed out (TC1)

attack_path.note: Untrusted web content is fetched during research.
Agent saves 'useful' content as memory via memory.save; free text, no provenance, no review.
At the next session start, the (possibly poisoned) memory is recalled and injected into the system prompt.
Recalled memory, treated as the user's own instruction per prompt.md line 4, directs the agent to read confidential drive documents.
Recalled memory directs the agent to email the drive content to an address of the attacker's choosing; mail.send requires no approval.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: New data sources feeding memory.save, new egress-capable tools, wider drive scope, or any future approval/allowlist control being added and later removed or bypassed.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to save anything useful from research as memory via memory.save, with no restriction on source trust.
Instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions, laundering untrusted content to trusted status every session.
memory.save accepts free text with no provenance and is never reviewed by the user; mail.send can send to any address without approval; drive.read covers the full drive including confidential files.

recommendations.action: Never treat recalled memory content as an instruction; present it as labeled, non-authoritative data and re-derive actions only from the authenticated user's current turn.
Require raw-action human approval, reviewed individually, for mail.send, especially to recipients not already in the user's contact list.
Add provenance/taint tags to memory entries, enforced at the store, distinguishing user-authored instructions from agent-derived research notes.
Scope drive.read to only what a research session needs, and add a recipient allowlist for mail.send bound to the user's known contacts.

findings.title: No attributable record of memory writes or sensitive tool calls (repudiation)

forecast.watch_signal: Any move toward higher-volume or longer-horizon autonomous operation without adding tamper-evident logging of memory writes, drive reads, and email sends.

evidence.observation: memory.save accepts free text. There is no provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them.
Recalled memories are treated as instructions with no record distinguishing their origin from the user's own words.

recommendations.action: Log every memory write and every sensitive tool call (drive.read, mail.send) with tamper-evident provenance tied to the triggering session and content source, so a poisoning incident can be investigated after the fact.
Periodically surface saved memories to the user for review and pruning.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe any identity verification mechanism for the agent itself (for example a signed agent identity); insufficient evidence to assess.
Artifacts do not state whether memory.save or mail.send are rate limited, or whether unattended step or runtime limits exist; cannot assess loop or cost-harvesting risk.

The agent does not gain capabilities beyond those already granted (memory.save, mail.send, drive.read); the harm is misuse of existing permissions via goal hijacking, captured as agentic_class goal_manipulation on finding.memory_poisoning_exfil, not a privilege escalation.

The web source is anonymous and outside the assessed system; non-repudiation of arbitrary external web content is not a property this design can provide, and the operative risk is trust elevation, captured in finding.memory_poisoning_exfil.
The external mail recipient is outside the assessed system; non-repudiation of a third-party recipient is out of scope for this agent's own design.
Artifacts do not describe any channel through which memory store contents could be read back by a party other than this agent; insufficient evidence beyond the tampering path already captured.
Artifacts do not state a cap on the number or size of memory entries memory.save can create.
Only drive.read is declared for this agent; no write or delete capability on the drive is in scope, so the agent itself cannot tamper with its contents.
Read-only access with no evidence of volume-based exhaustion risk to the drive store from this agent's usage pattern.
This flow carries content into the agent; it is not a channel through which internal data is exposed outward.
Artifacts do not state any limit on the volume or frequency of web fetches during research.
This flow carries stored content into the agent's context; it is not a channel through which data leaves the system.
Artifacts do not state a limit on the number or size of memories injected at session start.
No evidence of in-transit tampering risk is presented for this outbound channel to the user's own mail provider.
Artifacts do not state a rate limit on mail.send.

rating.rationale: The design launders untrusted web content into trusted instructions through an unreviewed, unprovenanced memory store (TC5), and those poisoned instructions can direct the agent to read the user's confidential drive and email it to any address with no approval (TC1 completing the chain). This gives critical inherent and residual risk for finding.memory_poisoning_exfil: every protective measure identified (provenance tagging, raw-action approval, recipient allowlist, treating recall as data not instructions) is absent and recorded only as a recommendation, so no control credit applies. The same absence of provenance and logging also leaves no attributable record of agent actions (finding.no_audit_trail, high, capped per rubric 5a). Forecast equals residual at critical because the primary finding is already at the ceiling; no named trigger can raise it further. The single highest-leverage fix is to stop treating recalled memory as an instruction and to gate mail.send behind raw-action, low-volume human approval.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP configuration, tool manifest, or runtime policy file was provided; capability scope (for example, the exact extent of drive.read or the memory.save schema) is inferred from the runtime notes, which lowers confidence on exact data sensitivity in places.

Autonomy limits (max unattended steps, max runtime, spawning, self-configuration) are not stated in the artifacts; autonomy.level is inferred as A3_act_then_report from the absence of any described approval gate, and this inference should be confirmed against the actual orchestration configuration.
